questions.answer: Working dir holds edits, staging (add) selects what goes next, commit snapshots staged changes, push shares to remote. Branches isolate work; merge combines.
questions.question: Explain working dir -> stage -> commit -> remote.

questions.answer: pull = fetch + merge from remote into current branch. Push publishes local commits. Pull before starting and before pushing to avoid rejected/diverged histories.
questions.question: git pull vs git push?

questions.answer: Blind git add . stages scratch/secret files. Fix: stage intentionally (git add src/), keep .gitignore from day one, and use git rm --cached to untrack committed junk.

questions.answer: Push was rejected because remote moved ahead (or local behind). Fix: git pull origin main (resolve merges), then push. Pulling often prevents it.
